words.gloss: In the midst of an action
like those who have completely failed

literal: In action, avoid ruining the action; the world has abandoned those who leave their work unfinished, just like those who have completely failed.
translation: Avoid slacking or ruining an undertaking while in the midst of it; the world will abandon those who leave their work incomplete, just as it abandons those who are completely ruined.
modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்யும்போது சோர்வடைந்து அச்செயலைக் கெடுத்துவிடுவதைத் தவிர்க்க வேண்டும். அவ்வாறு செய்யாமல் வேலையை அரைகுறையாக விட்டுவிடுபவர்களை, முற்றிலும் அழிந்துபோனவர்களை உலகம் கைவிடுவது போல, உலகமும் கைவிட்டுவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of completing any undertaken task without slacking or leaving it unfinished. The poet advises that once an action is started ('வினைக்கண்'), one must guard against ('ஓம்பல்') ruining it ('வினைகெடல்') through laziness or loss of enthusiasm. If a person leaves their work incomplete ('வினைக்குறை'), the world will abandon them ('தீர்ந்தன்று உலகு') just as it completely ignores and abandons those who have already failed or lost everything ('தீர்ந்தாரின்'). Success lies not just in starting, but in carrying a task through to its absolute completion.
